data.body:
PLAN REVIEW RETURNED BLOCK WITH TWO FINDINGS. BOTH ACCEPTED — one was a factual error of mine, and I
verified it in source before conceding rather than deferring to the reviewer.

FINDING 1 (impact 0.8) — the plan contradicted ITSELF on the headroom threshold. Approach said assert
`< 700` "same as the existing seam tests"; Testing said assert `< 800` now and let the extraction
tickets tighten. Both were mine, in the same document. RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF STAGING, because the
staged form is the only one that lands: the two files this guard covers are ABOVE 700 TODAY
(workflow_ops.py 794, config.py 793), so a `< 700` assertion lands RED. This ticket now asserts
`< 800` — still a real guard, it catches the next commit that would breach the hard cap — and each
sibling EXTRACTION ticket tightens its own file to `< 700` in the same change that creates the
headroom. Every ticket stays independently landable. `< 700` remains the POLICY number, with its
calibration retained (median per-commit delta ~+10, mean ~+18, p90 ~+45, worst +185 on f373cf4a6e).

FINDING 2 (impact 1.0) — I ASSERTED A STALE DOCSTRING THAT IS NOT STALE. My Scope listed
`plan_review_recovery.py:8` as needing a stale-docstring correction. VERIFIED IN SOURCE: that
docstring says three of the five finalize_verdict call sites "live in THIS CLUSTER", and there are
exactly three in that file — `:223`, `:297`, `:336`. It is ACCURATE. I had mentally attributed
test_gate_dispatch_seam.py's wording to it.
The genuinely stale text is test_gate_dispatch_seam.py's own ASSERTION MESSAGE, which asserts on
`gate_dispatch.py` while describing "its three finalize_verdict call sites" — gate_dispatch now holds
ZERO of them. (Its docstring at :3-5 reads as historical narration of the pre-split state, so it is
defensible; the assertion message is not.) Scope and file_impact corrected: plan_review_recovery.py
REMOVED from both, and the AC retargeted to the assertion message, naming the files that actually
hold the sites — plan_review_recovery.py (3) and plan_review/workflow_ops.py (2).

This is worth noting as a process point: the finding I got wrong was one I had asserted CONFIDENTLY
and repeated across three tickets and a session comment. The reviewer caught it by doing the one thing
I had not — reading the cited line. Editing file_impact and the description is safe here because the
attestation was BLOCK and therefore unsigned; nothing was destroyed.
